slides.title: Raise prices in 2027 where we have pricing power, and hold SMB until we have tested it

paragraphs.text: Raise prices in 2027 where we have pricing power, and hold SMB until we have tested it
Recommendation to the CEO and leadership team for the December 2026 pricing decision
Prepared November 2026 from the internal briefing pack only. No outside research was used.
All company figures are synthetic benchmark data. ARR figures are $M; churn is monthly logo churn unless stated.

slides.title: Yes, raise prices in 2027, but only for mid-market and enterprise. Hold SMB, test it, and fix the promotion cohort with onboarding, not price

paragraphs.text: Yes, raise prices in 2027, but only for mid-market and enterprise. Hold SMB, test it, and fix the promotion cohort with onboarding, not price
Churn is rising in one place. About 90% of the SMB rise (2.0% → 3.1% a month) comes from the 2,100 customers who joined on the 2025 half-price promotion. Other SMB customers moved from 2.0% to 2.1%.
The promotion cohort is an onboarding problem. Only 41% got started properly (72% for other cohorts), and most leavers went within two months of the discount ending.
Mid-market and enterprise can take an increase. Their NRR is 112% and 118%, a +10% list test had no significant effect on conversion, and Inkwell is absent above 200 seats.
SMB is the open question. Inkwell sells at $9 against our $15. A 12% SMB increase adds about $1.2M if customers react as they did in 2023, and nothing if they react twice as strongly.
The CFO's $10.3M is $7.6M before any churn response, because only part of the ARR renews in 2027 and enterprise increases are capped.
Mid-market: +10% list price at renewal (the tested level).
Enterprise: up to the 7% cap where contracts cap increases; up to +10% elsewhere.
SMB: hold $15 in H1 and split-test +8% in Q1. Extend it to H2 renewals only if churn holds.
Promotion cohort: no increase. Run an onboarding programme aimed at returning it to normal SMB churn.
plus up to $0.7M if the SMB test passes
growth from existing customers. About $0.6M of new-customer ARR reaches 15%
Trade-off: on paper this is $0.8–2.0M less 2027 ARR than the CFO's plan. In return, we avoid betting the 5,900-customer SMB base on a reaction we have not measured.
Source: Palisade briefing pack (2026), synthetic benchmark data.

slides.title: Churn is rising almost entirely in SMB, and within SMB almost entirely among customers who joined on the 2025 promotion

paragraphs.text: Churn is rising almost entirely in SMB, and within SMB almost entirely among customers who joined on the 2025 promotion
Monthly logo churn by group, %, H1 2025 vs H1 2026
If the promotion cohort churned like other SMB customers, SMB churn would be 2.1%, not 3.1%. About 1.0 of the 1.1-point rise is the cohort.
Regular SMB customers have barely moved (2.0% → 2.1%), even after Inkwell's launch in October 2025.
Mid-market is up from a low base (0.6% → 0.8%). Watch it, but it is not the driver. Enterprise is flat.
The board dashboard's "1.4% → 2.3%" does not define its measure and cannot be reconciled with these figures (appendix). Decide on segment logo churn.

The blended rise (19% → 34%) is a mix effect. The promotion cohort's share of churners grew, and 52% of those churners cite price. Regular SMB churners are flat at 18%.
Most cohort leavers went within two months of the 50% discount ending. For them, the "price" answer is the jump back to full price, not our list level.
So what: the CFO is right that this is mostly an onboarding problem. It also means this cohort will not absorb a further increase in 2027.

slides.title: SMB is now exposed on price. A 12% increase pays off only if customers react less than twice as strongly as they did in 2023, and we cannot yet tell

paragraphs.text: SMB is now exposed on price. A 12% increase pays off only if customers react less than twice as strongly as they did in 2023, and we cannot yet tell
List price per user per month, $
Net 2027 ARR effect of +12% on all SMB, by strength of churn reaction, $M
Win rate vs Inkwell in SMB: 51% → 38% (H1 2025 → H1 2026).
2023 precedent: +8% at renewal lifted SMB churn from 1.8% to 2.3% for six months, then it settled at 1.9%. That was before Inkwell existed.
Pointing the other way: regular SMB churners citing price are flat (18% vs 19%).

Gross gain is 12% × $21.0M = $2.5M. The 2023 response, scaled to 12%, means +0.75 pts of churn for six months and +0.15 pts after, losing about 5.4% of SMB customers. Break-even is about twice the 2023 reaction. The win-rate drop makes that plausible but not proven.
Source: Palisade briefing pack (2026), synthetic benchmark data.

slides.title: Recommended plan: raise mid-market and enterprise prices at renewal, hold the SMB list price while we test it, and onboard the promotion cohort

paragraphs.text: Recommended plan: raise mid-market and enterprise prices at renewal, hold the SMB list price while we test it, and onboard the promotion cohort
+10% list price at renewal from January. 85% of mid-market ARR ($34.9M) renews in 2027.
NRR 112%. The +10% test showed no significant effect. Break-even needs churn to roughly double.
Up to the 7% cap on capped contracts; up to +10% on uncapped renewals, under each contract's terms. 40% renews in 2027.
NRR 118%, churn 0.2%. Customers stay for integrations and audit trail.
Hold $15 in H1. In Q1, split-test +8% on half of renewals. If the test passes, apply +8% to H2 renewals.
Inkwell at $9; win rate down to 38%. Whether customers react like 2023 or twice as strongly decides whether 12% pays.
No increase in 2027. Run an onboarding programme for customers sending fewer than five documents a month.
41% got started properly. Leavers went when the discount ended. Price would accelerate it.

Total: +$4.3M of 2027 ARR from price in the plan, with up to +$1.7M of upside if the SMB test passes and onboarding works. We also recommend not repeating untargeted 50%-off promotions for new self-serve customers.
Source: Palisade briefing pack (2026), synthetic benchmark data.

slides.title: Onboarding can bring SMB churn back to about 2.1%, not halve it. Plan around the promotion cohort, not the headline claim

paragraphs.text: Onboarding can bring SMB churn back to about 2.1%, not halve it. Plan around the promotion cohort, not the headline claim
The cohort is $4.4M of ARR. At ~4.9% a month it loses about 45% of that over 12 months; at 2.1%, about 22%.
Closing that gap retains up to ~$1.0M of ARR. That is a real prize, but not a substitute for price.
Caveat: much of the H1 2026 churn was the cliff when the discount ended. The survivors may already churn less, so the gain could be smaller.
Target: cohort churn converging on the regular SMB rate (~2.1%) by mid-2027, tracked monthly.
Cohort fixed: churns like regular SMB
Halving 3.1% means 1.55%. That would need regular SMB customers to fall well below the 1.8–2.0% range SMB has run at since 2023, not just to fix the promotion cohort.
Source: Palisade briefing pack (2026), synthetic benchmark data.

slides.title: How the main figures were calculated

paragraphs.text: How the main figures were calculated
12% × $86.0M = $10.3M. This assumes every dollar of ARR reprices in 2027 at the full 12%.
SMB 12% × $21.0M = $2.52M; mid-market 12% × 85% × $41.0M = $4.18M; enterprise renewing $9.6M (40% of $24.0M): 60% capped at 7% = $0.40M, plus 40% at 12% = $0.46M. Total $7.57M.
2023: +8% gave +0.5 pts for six months, then +0.1 pts. Scaled linearly to 12%: +0.75 pts × 6 months + 0.15 pts × 6 months = 5.4% of customers lost, × $23.5M repriced ARR = $1.27M (×2 = $2.54M).
Mid-market 10% × $34.85M = $3.49M. Enterprise: $5.76M capped at 7% = $0.40M, plus $3.84M at 10% = $0.38M. Total $4.27M.
+8% on roughly half of regular SMB ARR (renewing in H2): 8% × 50% × $16.6M ≈ $0.66M. Regular SMB ARR = $21.0M − $4.4M cohort.

Gain p is cancelled when the share of customers lost in the year reaches p ÷ (1 + p). Mid-market at 10%: 9.1% a year ≈ +0.8 pts a month. SMB at 8%: 7.4% ≈ +0.6 pts. SMB at 12%: 10.7%, about twice the 2023 response.
12-month retention at 4.9% a month = 55%; at 2.1% = 78%. Difference × $4.4M ≈ $1.0M.

About 1,900 customers per arm for three months at a 2.1% base rate gives a standard error of about 0.27 pts on the difference. A 0.6-pt reaction is about 2.2 standard errors (detectable); a 0.3-pt reaction is about 1.1 (not). This assumes most test customers renew within Q1, which needs monthly plans; fewer renewals means a weaker test.
Source: Palisade briefing pack (2026), synthetic benchmark data.

paragraphs.text: APPENDIX B · DATA CAVEATS AND CHOICES
The board churn figure cannot be reproduced. This page also lists the choices made where the briefing pack was silent
Choices made where the pack was silent
Mid-market increase set at 10%, the tested level, rather than 12%.
SMB test at +8%, the 2023 level, so the 2023 response is a usable benchmark.
Enterprise uncapped renewals at up to +10%, matching mid-market. Actual terms vary by contract.
2027 enterprise renewals assumed 60% capped, the same share as the whole enterprise book.
2027 NRR before price assumed equal to trailing 12-month NRR. The SMB figure (94%) includes the promotion cliff, so it is probably conservative.
Renewals spread evenly through the year, so about half of SMB ARR renews in H2.
Promotion-cohort churn (4.9%) is implied from blended and regular SMB rates, weighted by mid-2026 counts.
Not in the pack, so not modelled: new-customer bookings, gross margin, and the cost of the onboarding programme.
Weighted with mid-2026 customer counts and ARR from Table 1. None of the obvious definitions gives 1.4% → 2.3%. Until Finance defines the figure, it should not be used for this decision.
SMB test shows little reaction → extend +8% to H2 SMB renewals (already in the rule).
Mid-market renewals react much more than the new-sign-up test suggested → pause at the tripwire.
New-customer bookings fall short of ~$0.6M → revisit the 12% mid-market option ($0.7M).
Source: Palisade briefing pack (2026), synthetic benchmark data.
